headword: {竹取物語|たけとりものがたり}
gloss: The Tale of the Bamboo Cutter (early Heian tale)

definitions.gloss: The Tale of the Bamboo Cutter
definitions.explanation: Japan's oldest surviving prose tale, written in the early Heian period (around the 9th–10th century) by an unknown author. An old bamboo cutter finds a tiny girl inside a glowing bamboo stalk; she grows into the beautiful かぐや{姫|ひめ}, sets impossible tasks for her suitors, and finally returns to the moon.

examples.japanese: {竹取物語|たけとりものがたり}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧{最古|さいこ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{物語|ものがたり}→物語：03634_monogatari⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われる→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: The Tale of the Bamboo Cutter is said to be Japan's oldest tale.

examples.english: In The Tale of the Bamboo Cutter, Princess Kaguya returns to the moon on the night of a full moon.

notes:
Every Japanese child knows the story as the picture book かぐや⟦{姫|ひめ}→姫：12233_hime⟧, and every student reads its opening in classical Japanese class. The ⟦{源氏物語|げんじものがたり}→源氏物語：31025_genjimonogatari⟧ itself calls it "the ancestor of tales."

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- ⟦{今|いま}→今：00945_ima⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧、⟦{竹取|たけとり}→竹取：28465_taketori⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{翁|おきな}といふものありけり: "Long ago there was an old man called the bamboo cutter" — the famous opening line
- かぐや⟦{姫|ひめ}→姫：12233_hime⟧: Princess Kaguya, the heroine; also a nickname for an unattainable beauty
- {無理難題|むりなんだい}: an impossible demand, like the tasks she set her suitors

CULTURAL NOTE:
Several episodes end in puns. One prince brings back a fake begging bowl (⟦{鉢|はち}→鉢：29581_hachi⟧), throws it away, and keeps courting — "throwing away his shame" (⟦{恥|はじ}→恥：12636_haji⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{捨|す}てる→捨てる：00892_suteru⟧). The tale ends by naming Mount Fuji ({富士|ふじ}) after the elixir of immortality (⟦{不死|ふし}→不死：11711_fushi⟧) burned on its summit.
